newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan "Big Bang" needed sooner than planned-report.
newsitem.headline: Japan "Big Bang" needed sooner than planned-report.

text.p: The proposed "Big Bang" reforms of Japan's financial markets should be carried out sooner than planned, as partial reforms could lead to a further "hollowing" of Tokyo markets, a Japanese think tank said.

The Japan Research Institute said in a report issued this week that unless recently proposed deregulation of the Tokyo foreign exchange market in 1998 was carried out in conjunction with wider financial reforms, it could actually worsen the very situation it is designed to improve.
"Having 2001 as a goal (for the "Big Bang") is too late," the report said.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has vowed to carry out a sweeping reform of Japanese markets by 2001.

The report cited the forex deregulation plan proposed last December, which calls for scrapping the current rule limiting forex transactions to authorised foreign exchange banks and abolishing the system of getting permission and giving prior notification for cross-border capital transactions.

Noting that this means Japanese financial institutions and corporations would be able to deal directly with their overseas counterparts, the report said Japanese markets could end up at a marked disadvantage without additional financial reforms.

Should Japanese institutions be unable to offer the same range of financial products, and at prices competitive with overseas counterparts, it would be natural for both Japanese and other investors to do their business abroad, it added.
Additional burdens are posed by comparatively high fees for market transactions in Japan, as well as a securities transaction tax, the report noted.
These factors, along with regulations limiting the development of products such as derivatives, are often cited to explain the shift of business from Tokyo to overseas centres.

The report strongly recommended relaxing regulations concerning derivatives, sales of negotiable securities and insurance products, and the issuing of commercial paper and asset-backed securities, among others. It also recommended doing away with the securities transaction tax.

Noting differences in tax and accounting standards between Japan and other countries, the report also said: "To prevent further hollowing, bringing Japan in line with international standards is an important and urgent issue."
